newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS - Itau wins Brazil's first state bank sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Itau wins Brazil's first state bank sale.

text.p: Brazil kicked off its ambitious state bank privatization drive Thursday with the sale of Rio de Janeiro's Banerj to bank Banco Itau for 311.1 million reais ($291 million).
Itau's purchase of Banerj, which was widely expected, takes the bank's total assets to 31 billion reais, just shy of Bradesco, Brazil's largest privately owned bank with 35 billion reais in assets.
"The privatization of Banerj is vital for the process of evaluating other state banks," said Finance Ministry Executive Secretary Pedro Parente.

At least four other banks, including federally owned Banco Meridional, are expected to be sold in the next few years. The second on the list is Minas Gerais state bank Credireal, due to be sold off in the second half of the year.
The largest state bank slated for the auction block is Banespa, Sao Paulo's troubled state bank whose mammoth debt and shoddy bookeeping are now being sorted out by the federal government.
In a closed-envelope auction, Itau agreed to pay slightly more for Banerj than the bank's base price of 310 million reais.
The acquisition will add 4.5 billion reais to Itau's assets.
Bradesco, BCN and Cia. de Investimento Latino-Americana, owned by a foreign bank and represented by local Banco Pactual, had been expected to bid for Banerj.

But only Itau presented a proposal to buy the bank. Analysts said Itau had a competitive reason to buy the bank if only to keep it from Bradesco, which would have grown considerably bigger than Itau if it purchased Banerj.

Itau vice-president Olavo Bueno said the bank bought Banerj because of its strong presence in Rio de Janeiro. Banerj adds 193 branches to Itau's network of about 650 branches in the Brazilian southeastern state.
"Banerj brings new retail clients which fits into Itau's main strategy," Bueno said.
The state of Rio de Janeiro had been trying to sell Banerj since December 1996, but the sale was delayed due to legal challenges and debt worries.

The sell-off only took place after the Senate approved a 3.09 billion reais loan to Rio state to pay off Banerj's pension and payroll-related debts. The loan was key to make the bank attractive to investors.
Also to facilitate the sale, the state cut Banerj's base price to 310 million reais from 480 million reais, which was set last year.

It also allowed the buyer to pay for 100 percent of the bank's auction price with federal and state privatization bonds, which made the bank even cheaper as those bonds are traded at 60-70 percent of their face value.
Banerj has been under Central Bank control since December 1994 but has been managed on a day-to-day basis by private bank Banco Bozano, Simonsen on behalf of the Central Bank since January 1996.
Bozano was hired to ready the bank for privatization.

In Bozano's hands, Banerj showed improved results. Time deposits rose 6.07 percent to 1.163 billion reais in December last year from 1.096 billion reais in 1995, while savings accounts at the bank increased 20.53 percent to 931.3 million reais from 772.7 million reais in the same period.
Revenues with banking services jumped 122.98 percent to 12.5 million reais from 5.6 million reais.
((--Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 2485412))
